implementation_notes: Go has no message envelope type in the standard library, so the idiomatic realization is a plain struct: named header fields (or a small map with typed accessors) plus the payload kept as json.RawMessage so wrapping never re-marshals the body. Struct composition replaces the classic envelope class; on gRPC the transport already offers a metadata side channel (metadata.New and metadata.FromIncomingContext) so the body can stay untouched. Reach for a generated protobuf envelope (Any or a wrapped message) only when the wire contract is shared with non-Go services.
pitfalls: json.RawMessage aliases the input buffer: if the caller reuses or mutates that slice the wrapped payload changes underneath you - copy it when ownership is unclear.
A map[string]string header loses non-string metadata and accepts arbitrary producer-chosen keys; validate unknown keys at the seam instead of forwarding them into the domain.
encoding/json v1 matches struct fields case-insensitively and ignores unknown fields, so a header renamed by a producer silently lands in the default value - tag fields explicitly.
